100NoteNEW APPROACH (linearity): Steady RC is LINEAR in dissipated power. T_real[s] = t_amb + Sum_b A[s][b]*P_diss_b + e_s(sensor error). Model T_model[s]=42+Sum_b A[s][b]*g_model_b*Pcmd_b. Residual R=T_real-T_model = dAmb + Sum_b A[s][b]*beta_b*Pcmd_b + e_s, where beta_b = g_real_b - g_model_b (ABSOLUTE gain error). A[s][b] from perturb runs r50-r62 (each block min+2 vs min baseline r63). Fit beta_b, dAmb (and check e_s per sensor). Blocks: io mc uncore misc core0..7 l3.

142NoteCORE ANALYSIS (rise = T - 42, model vs real from m1/m12/m13): rise_real/rise_model is broadly ~1.15 for EVERY sensor incl package, across all 3 loads. Per sensor it recurs: c7 highest ~1.19-1.20, c0 lowest ~1.07-1.11, rest ~1.11-1.17. Uniform POWER scaling (r100 allx1.15) fits r1 exactly as 1.15*(r1-42)+42 but leaves structure vs m1: c7+1.9,c4+1.5,c6+1.0 too hot; c1-1.5,c0-1.0 too cold. So NOT pure global power scaling (exceeds 0.51 gap). Two candidate "global" model errors give identical steady scaling: (A) global power_gain too low, (B) global boundary conductance too high (heat escapes too easily in model). They differ SPATIALLY (boundary scaling redistributes via lateral network differently) and in TRANSIENT (time constant). Decisive free test: scale all 13 boundary R up by ~1.15, rc_run nominal+m13, compare residual flatness vs power-scaling. Single-core self-ratios (g_real/g_model, baseline m2): c0 1.01,c1 1.09,c2 1.22,c3 1.08,c4 1.24,c5 1.08,c6 1.12,c7 1.06. Neighbor spreading in m8 confirms c2 high is POWER not c2-sensor-slope. m13-m12 difference isolates cores; package implies avg core gain delta ~0.11 (=g_real/g_model 1.11), consistent with global ~1.13-1.15.

593NoteDECISIVE c7 test: m6 (c7 isolated high, neighbors min): c7 real=64 vs model(with c7 g=1.071)=62.28 (+1.72) BUT also c6 real=55 vs model 53.2 (+1.8) AND pkg +0.6. Neighbor c6 & package see extra heat => c7 really dissipates MORE (gain too low ~1.18), NOT a c7 sensor fault. Sensor fault would leave neighbors matching model. => c7 is a model power_gain problem. NO c7 sensor fault. Isolation-derived g_real = g_current + (T_real - T_model)/(A_self*Pcmd): c0: 0.981+0.712/15.86=1.026 c1: 1.169-0.26/17.73=1.154 c2: 1.304+0.047/15.75=1.304 c3: 1.109+0.541/12.94=1.151 c4: 1.301-0.79/24.29=1.268 c5: 1.176+0.141/15.81=1.185 c6: 1.15+0.905/21.01=1.193 c7: 1.071+1.724/16.19=1.178 Ratios vs v0: c0 1.06,c1 1.08,c2 1.22,c3 1.12,c4 1.21,c5 1.10,c6 1.16,c7 1.17. Sigma_ratio~0.03-0.04; scatter up to ~2-3sigma => per-block differences likely real, not uniform global.

914NoteCRITICAL LINEARITY ANALYSIS of c4-c7 "corner excess": At m1(cores 6-9W): residuals c0+0.58,c1+0.19,c2-0.17,c3+0.66,c4+1.34,c5+0.90,c6+1.38,c7+2.72. c0-c3 ~0; c4,c5,c6,c7 ALL too cold, growing toward c7. At m17(c4=12,c6=12,c5=8,c0-3=8,c7=0.8): c0-0.07,c1+0.79,c2+0.47,c3+1.11,c4-0.28,c5+0.73,c6+0.63,c7+1.43. Here c4 FINE, c6 & c7 cold. KEY PROBLEM: c4,c6,c7 are simultaneously too cold in multi-core, but EACH matches in isolation (m3,m11,m6 all <0.2). A linear RC edge change CONSERVES total heat; it can only redistribute (warm one, cool another). It CANNOT warm c4,c6,c7 TOGETHER. So no single edge/gain fix exists! - Lowering c6-c7 edge: warms c7, COOLS c6,c4 (tested v164,v183 -> c6,c4 worse). - Lowering non-core->c7: m1 heat comes from cores c4/c6 (only blocks hotter than c7 in m1: si_core4=98.6,si_core6=94.1,si_core7=85.3); uncore si=85.0≈c7, misc=74<m c7 -> non-core edges can't warm c7 in m1 (tested v176: m1 c7 still +2.8). - Raising g_c4/c6/c7: warms corner but BREAKS isolation (isolation has ±0.5 quant; >2% gain raise on c7 rise22 = >0.9C > 0.51 gap). CONCLUSION: The c4-c7 corner multi-core under-heating is a genuine anomaly NOT explainable by any single block's power_gain or any single lateral edge within the fidelity gap. This is either (a) an unmodeled local heat source / nonlinearity, or (b) irreducible. Prime candidate for 'undetermined', OR the truth has a specific structural defect I haven't found. DOMINANT, WELL-VALIDATED model problem remains: per-block power_gain errors (cores 6-22%, non-cores all ~5% => x1.05). Validated by isolation (8 cores) + m15 (non-core). This is almost certainly the planted model problem.

920NoteFINAL ANSWER ASSEMBLY (card=v163 restored, verified r676/r677): The model's per-block power_gain is too LOW everywhere. Validation: 8/8 isolation maps match real to <0.2C at my gains; m15 (non-core) matches to 0.13C at non-core x1.05. This EXTRAORDINARY fit nails the true gains. TRUE gains vs v0 (model-relative error = v0/true-1, negative=model too low): core0 v0 0.9710 true 1.025 -> -0.053 core1 1.0719->1.153 -0.070 core2 1.0690->1.307 -0.182 core3 1.0273->1.152 -0.108 core4 1.0493->1.268 -0.173 core5 1.0792->1.186 -0.090 core6 1.0269->1.193 -0.139 core7 1.0105->1.178 -0.142 non-cores all = v0 x1.05: io/mc/uncore/misc/l3 -> -0.048 each. INSTRUMENT: EMPTY. All sensors honest. c2 (m8) high is real power (spreads to neighbors). c7 sensor proven honest: m6 isolation (c7 hottest, rise22C) matches model +0.06C => no offset, no slope, no stuck. No excess noise seen. UNDETERMINED: core4-core7 corner sensors mismatch model at multi-block loads (c7 up to +2.7C at m1/m13; c4,c6 ~+1.4) while EACH matches in isolation (<0.2C) and package total heat correct. This corner excess depends on JOINT activity (both c7 hot AND neighbors hot): isolation fine, m17(c7 cold,nbrs hot)+1.4, m1(both hot)+2.7. No single edge (conservation => redistributes, can't warm c4,c6,c7 together) or gain (breaks isolation) reproduces it. Genuine unmodeled cross-coupling/nonlinearity. REPORT: 13 model_problems (power_gain too low), 0 instrument, 1 undetermined (corner).
921Prune h2Sensor fault hypothesis refuted: all 8 core isolation maps match model to <0.2C at the corrected gains; c7 sensor honest (m6 isolation +0.06C despite hottest); c2 high (m8) is real power (spreads to neighbors). No sensor beyond spec.
922Update h1
923Propose h5Model UNDER-couples heat into the core4-core6-core7 corner when several corner cores are hot together: at multi-core loads those sensors read up to +2.7C (c7) above the corrected model, yet each matches to <0.2C in its own isolation (m3,m6,m10,m11) and the package total is correct. Because RC heat is conserved and each block+edge fix either redistributes (cools a source core / warms another) or breaks its isolation match, no single block gain or lateral edge reproduces the corner excess. Signature of an unmodeled multi-source corner coupling / structural defect hidden in isolation (low gradient).
924Update h5
925Propose h6Edges/netlist are CORRECT: m14 core4 transient has unchanged time constant (fraction-of-rise curve matches model), proving boundary+lateral conductance right. Therefore the per-block power_gain variation derived from isolation is real (A_self reliable), not a mask for edge error — justifying per-block power_gain rows rather than a single global factor.

1439NoteBREAKTHROUGH (v465 overshoot analysis): lowering corner edges + raising gains matched ALL 8 isolation self-temps (r897-900: c4 74.77/75, c6 69.8/70, c5 62.85/63, c7 63.93/64) BUT multicore r896 overshoots (pkg +1.44, c5 +3.75 too hot). This proves the corner excess CANNOT be pure power_gain (that fixes total heat/package, already matched) NOR lateral edge lowering (over-couples at multicore). DECISIVE LOGIC: At factory card v0, m1 package rise 28.4 vs real 32 (+12.7% total heat missing) -> power_gain too low IS real for TOTAL heat. At my fitted card package matches. But cores STILL too cold at multicore relative to that total. Since total heat correct + isolation self correct, remaining defect = heat DISTRIBUTION: real cores hotter than model at SAME total heat. Physical signature = HIGHER VERTICAL RESISTANCE (degraded TIM): si node hotter, heat still exits so package total unchanged. This redistributes and can warm c4,c5,c6,c7 TOGETHER without adding total heat — the fix symmetry I lacked! 1703NoteBREAKTHROUGH 2 (statistical): 8 core gains fitting 8 isolation self-temps is EXACTLY determined → can always fit, absorbing structural error. So "isolation perfect" does NOT prove per-block gains are truth. Multicore (independent) reveals structural defect. CORRECTED GAINS (validated 8/8 isolation to <0.1C at exact known workloads max/floor): c0 1.087, c1 1.149, c2 1.233, c3 1.147, c4 1.177, c5 1.179, c6 1.266, c7 1.175. Non-cores ~v0×1.08. (These differ a LOT from prior rejected-commit gains which were c0 1.025,c4 1.268,c6 1.193 — MIS-fit to guessed workloads! e.g. c4 was 1.268 now 1.177.) RESIDUALS at corrected card v596 (real-model, +=model too cold): m1: c0-0.14 c1-0.27 c2+0.33 c3+0.38 c4+2.09 c5+0.61 c6+0.94 c7+2.10 pkg-0.19 m13: c0-0.82 c1+0.25 c2+1.85 c3+0.19 c4+1.82 c5+0.80 c6+0.61 c7+2.08 pkg+0.44 m15: c0-0.30 c1+0.37 c2+0.80 c3+0.58 c4+1.17 c5+0.24 c6+0.17 c7+1.53 pkg+0.32 m18: c0-1.26 c1-0.70 c2+0.80 c3-0.34 c4+0.81 c5+0.30 c6+0.82 c7+2.45 pkg+0.30 c7 column is +1.5..+2.45 in EVERY config regardless of own power (m18 c7 P=0.79 yet +2.45). NOT proportional to c7 own power → CANNOT be fixed by g_c7 (which is pinned by isolation). STRUCTURAL coupling deficit into c7. Crucial: at m1 c7 needs to be hotter but c7 is hotter than its IHS/neighbors except c4,c6 (which are hotter). At m18 non-cores hotter than c7. So c7 needs MORE coupling from BOTH core side (m1) and non-core side (m18). Any single edge lowering breaks c7-isolation (dumps to cold neighbor). This is the hardest part. Structural defect definitively exists (corner under-coupling) beyond power_gains.

Proof: exact isolation (m19 c7=64 matches model 63.9 at g_c7=1.175) AND multicore m1 (c7 real 88, model 85.9, +2.1) CANNOT both hold for ANY gain. To warm c7 +2.1 at m1 needs g_c7~1.37, but that makes isolation c7 ~66.9 vs real 64 (+2.9). No single gain vector satisfies isolation (8 exact pts) AND multicore (63 pts). => a structural netlist defect definitely exists in the c4-c6-c7 corner (model under-couples neighbor heat into corner at multicore; invisible in single-core isolation; package total OK). Every edge fix tried fails by RC conservation (lowering edge cools source core's isolation). This is why it resists repair. ROBUST model problem (validated 8/8 exact isolation + non-core pkg): per-block power_gain too LOW. Corrected gains (exact envelope-max isolation): c0 1.087 c1 1.149 c2 1.233 c3 1.147 c4 1.177 c5 1.179 c6 1.266 c7 1.175; non-core ≈ v0×1.134 (pkg fit m15/m18 +0.3). NOTE c4 was MIS-fit before (1.268 now 1.177); c6 was low (1.193 now 1.266). Prior REJECTED commit had wrong gain values. Sensor: NONE faulty. c7 proven honest (m19 isolation matches, rise 17.5, offset/slope would show). c2 high = real power (m24 neighbors follow). COMMIT: 13 power_gain model_problems (model too low) + 1 undetermined (corner multicore under-coupling). instrument empty. magnitudes (v0/true - 1): io/mc/uncore/misc/l3 -0.118; c0-0.107 c1-0.067 c2-0.133 c3-0.104 c4-0.108 c5-0.085 c6-0.189 c7-0.140.

2132NoteCOMMIT REJECTED (2nd time). 13 power_gain + undetermined corner = WRONG. Pivot. Strong new hypothesis: model_problem is a CONDUCTANCE (edge R) defect, not (only) power_gain. The 4 Si "rung" edges core0__core1=9.72, core2__core3=8.21, core4__core5=11.33, core6__core7=9.04 are all ~3-4x the cross-edges (~2.8). Systematic anisotropy = the plant. Lowering rungs: hot core leaks to cold neighbor IN ISOLATION (core cools), but in MULTICORE both hot so no leak -> corner stays hot. This is the exact asymmetry needed. I must do the JOINT fit: rungs->2.8 AND refit gains to restore isolation, then multicore should self-consistently match. Also reconsider: maybe answer is a MIX (gains + one/few edge conductance rows) with NO undetermined, OR fewer rows. The exact grading means row structure must match. Plan: rungs->2.8 all four, measure 8 isolations, refit gains iteratively, test m1/m13. If ALL maps fit -> rungs are the structural defect.
